parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4 omits the central tree-component argument connecting the refinement graph to a nonzero signed sum of the original geometric pieces.

errors.description: The lower bound depends entirely on an asserted graph argument whose construction and inequality are not proved. It is repairable: since the pairing multigraph has at most n edges on n+1 vertices, it has a tree component; bipartition signs make each paired edge contribute a signed size difference, with only the possible unpaired part left over.
errors.quote: By a tree-component argument on the multigraph whose vertices are the original pieces $0,1,\dots,n$ and whose edges are the pairs $P_i$, there is a set $V_T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$ and signs $s:V_T\to\{\pm1\}$ such that the signed sum $\Xi:=\sum_{j\in V_T}s(j)\,q_j$ satisfies $|\Xi|\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted).

parsed.notes: The answer and upper-bound construction are correct and carefully justified. The sole omission is short and straightforward to supply, but it occurs in the essential lower-bound lemma, so the submitted proof is not fully complete.
